p.src: Baochai and Xiangyun, having settled all their plans, passed the night without further incident. The next day, Xiangyun invited Grandmother Jia and the others to admire the osmanthus blossoms. Grandmother Jia and the others all said, “Since she is in such high spirits, we must indulge her elegant fancy.” At noon, Grandmother Jia duly brought Lady Wang and Xifeng and, having invited Aunt Xue and the others as well, entered the garden. Grandmother Jia asked, “Which place would be best?” Lady Wang replied, “Whichever place pleases you, Old Lady, shall be the place.” Xifeng said, “Everything has already been laid out at Lotus-Fragrance Pavilion. The two osmanthus trees below the hillside are flowering beautifully, and the river water is a clear emerald. Would it not be airy and bright to sit in the pavilion in midstream? The sight of the water would refresh our eyes as well.” Hearing this, Grandmother Jia said, “That is very true.” With that, she led everyone toward Lotus-Fragrance Pavilion. Lotus-Fragrance Pavilion stood in the middle of the pond, with windows on all four sides and winding galleries to left and right. These galleries spanned the water to join the banks, while a twisting bamboo bridge provided a secluded approach at the rear. When they stepped onto the bamboo bridge, Xifeng hurried forward to support Grandmother Jia, saying, “Just stride out boldly, Old Ancestress. It is perfectly safe; bamboo bridges are supposed to creak and crack like this.”

p.src: Presently they entered the pavilion and saw two bamboo tables set outside the railing. Cups, chopsticks, and wine vessels stood on one, while the other held a tea whisk, tea bowls, and every kind of tea utensil. On one side, two or three maids were fanning a brazier to boil water for tea; on the other, several more maids were fanning another brazier to warm the wine. Delighted, Grandmother Jia promptly remarked, “How thoughtful to provide tea! And what an excellent spot—everything is so clean.” Xiangyun said with a smile, “Sister Bao helped me prepare all this.” Grandmother Jia said, “I have always said that this girl is meticulous and thinks everything through properly.” As she spoke, she noticed a couplet inlaid with mother-of-pearl on black-lacquered panels hanging from a pillar and ordered someone to read it aloud. p.src: Through shattered hibiscus shadows the orchid oars return; from deep lotus fragrance the bamboo bridge emerges.

p.src: After listening, Grandmother Jia looked up at the inscribed tablet and then turned to Aunt Xue. “When I was little,” she said, “we had a pavilion rather like this at home, called something like ‘Rosy-Cloud Pavilion.’ I was only about their age then and went there every day to play with my sisters. Who would have thought that one day I would lose my footing and fall in? I very nearly drowned. They finally managed to rescue me, but a wooden spike struck my head and split it open. That fingertip-sized hollow at my temple even now is the scar it left. Everyone feared that after being soaked and then exposed to the wind I could not possibly survive, yet somehow I recovered completely.” Before anyone else could speak, Xifeng laughed and said, “If you had not survived then, Old Ancestress, who would be enjoying all your great blessings now? Clearly, your blessings and longevity were already extraordinary when you were a child. The spirits arranged for that hollow to be knocked into your head so that it could hold them all. The God of Longevity originally had a hollow in his head too, but when it filled to the brim with countless blessings and endless years, it bulged outward instead.” Before she had even finished, Grandmother Jia and all the others were limp with laughter. Grandmother Jia laughed. “This little monkey has been spoiled beyond all bounds! Now you make me the butt of your jokes. I could tear that glib mouth of yours!” Xifeng replied with a laugh, “We shall be eating crabs shortly, and I feared their chill might settle in your stomach. I wanted to make you laugh and cheer you up; then, once you are happy, two extra crabs can do you no harm.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “From tomorrow on, I shall make you stay with me day and night. Frequent laughter cheers me, so you will not be allowed to go home.” Lady Wang said with a smile, “It is because you are so fond of her, Old Lady, that you have spoiled her into behaving this way. If you say such things as well, she will be more impudent than ever tomorrow.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “I like her this way. Besides, she is not a child who does not know how far she may go. When we are alone together as a family, this is just how we womenfolk ought to behave. So long as she never breaches proper decorum, that is enough. Why make her stand about as stiffly as an idol?”

p.src: As they spoke, they all entered the pavilion. After tea had been served, Xifeng busied herself setting up the tables and calling for cups and chopsticks. At the upper table sat Grandmother Jia, Aunt Xue, Baochai, Daiyu, and Baoyu; at the eastern table sat Shi Xiangyun, Lady Wang, Yingchun, Tanchun, and Xichun. A table near the western door had places nominally set for Li Wan and Xifeng, but neither dared sit down and instead waited upon the two tables of Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang. Xifeng ordered, “Do not bring too many crabs at once. Leave them in the steamer and bring ten now; when those are eaten, bring more.” She had water brought to wash her hands, then stood before Grandmother Jia and picked the crabmeat from the shell, offering the first portion to Aunt Xue. Aunt Xue said, “It tastes better when I break it open and eat it myself. There is no need to serve me.” Xifeng therefore presented it to Grandmother Jia. She gave the second portion to Baoyu and said, “Bring the wine piping hot.” She also sent the young maids to fetch mung-bean powder scented with chrysanthemum leaves and osmanthus stamens, to have ready for washing hands. After eating one crab to keep the guests company, Shi Xiangyun left her seat to attend to everyone. She then went outside and had two platefuls sent to Concubine Zhao and Concubine Zhou. Just then Xifeng came over and said, “You are not used to managing such things. Go and enjoy your meal. I will see to everything for you now and eat after the party is over.” Xiangyun would not agree. She also had two tables set on the veranda and invited Yuanyang, Hupo, Caixia, Caiyun, and Pinger to sit there. Yuanyang smiled at Xifeng and said, “Second Mistress, since you are waiting on everyone here, we can go and eat.” Xifeng said, “Go right ahead. Just leave everything to me.” At that, Shi Xiangyun returned to her seat. Xifeng and Li Wan also ate a little, merely for form’s sake. Xifeng then resumed overseeing matters. Presently she went out to the veranda, where Yuanyang and the others were eating merrily. When they saw her, they rose and said, “What have you come out here for again, Mistress? Let us enjoy ourselves for a little while too.” Xifeng laughed. “You impudent little Yuanyang, you are growing naughtier by the day! I do your work for you, yet instead of thanking me, you complain. Hurry and pour me a cup of wine.” Laughing, Yuanyang quickly poured a cup and held it to Xifeng’s lips. Xifeng tilted back her head and drank it. Hupo and Caixia together poured another cup and held it to Xifeng’s lips, and she drank that one too. Pinger had already picked out a shellful of roe and brought it over. Xifeng said, “Add plenty of ginger vinegar.” She ate it and then said with a laugh, “Sit down and carry on eating. I must be off.” Yuanyang laughed. “What shamelessness—eating our food!” Xifeng laughed. “Do stop your mischief. Do you know that your Second Master Lian has fallen in love with you and means to ask the Old Lady for you as his concubine?”

p.src: Yuanyang said, “Fie! Is that a proper thing for a mistress to say? If I do not smear your face with my fishy hands, I shall not have done you justice.” With that, she chased after Xifeng and tried to smear her face. Xifeng pleaded, “Dear sister, spare me just this once.” Hupo laughed. “Even if Yuanyang goes away, do you think Pinger will spare her? Just look at her! She has not eaten even two crabs, yet she has swallowed a whole saucer of vinegar. She certainly knows how to indulge her jealousy.” Pinger happened to be breaking open a crab packed with roe. Hearing this taunt, she thrust it toward Hupo’s face, laughing and scolding, “You wretched little gossip!” Hupo laughingly dodged aside. Pinger missed her and stumbled forward, smearing the crab squarely across Xifeng’s cheek. Xifeng had been bantering with Yuanyang and was taken completely by surprise. She gave a startled cry of “Oh!” No one could contain themselves, and they all burst into loud laughter. Xifeng too could not help laughing as she cursed, “You shameless hussy! Have you eaten yourself blind, smearing it about like that?” Pinger hurried over to wipe her cheek and then went herself to fetch water. Yuanyang said, “Amitabha! That is retribution.” Hearing the commotion from her table, Grandmother Jia repeatedly called out, “What have you seen that is so amusing? Tell us, so that we may laugh too.” Yuanyang and the others hurriedly called back with laughter, “Second Mistress came to snatch our crabs. Pinger grew angry and smeared her mistress’s face with crab roe. Mistress and maid are fighting.” Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang, and the others laughed when they heard this. Grandmother Jia laughed. “Poor thing! Just give her a few of those little legs and some meat from the apron, and that will settle it.” Yuanyang and the others laughingly assented, then called out, “There is a whole tableful of legs here. Second Mistress may eat as many as she likes!” After washing her face, Xifeng returned and waited upon Grandmother Jia and the others while they ate a little longer. Daiyu alone dared not eat much. After taking only a little meat from the claws, she left the table.

p.src: Before long, Grandmother Jia stopped eating, and only then did the company disperse. They all washed their hands; some admired the flowers, while others played with the water and watched the fish, amusing themselves for a time. Lady Wang said to Grandmother Jia, “It is windy here, and you have just eaten crab. You had better return to your room and rest, Old Lady. If you feel inclined, you can come and stroll here again tomorrow.” Grandmother Jia heard her and said with a smile, “Quite right. I was afraid that, while you were all enjoying yourselves, my leaving might spoil your pleasure. Since you put it that way, let us all go.” Then, turning back, she cautioned Xiangyun, “Do not let your Brother Bao and Sister Lin eat too much.” Xiangyun promised that she would not. She also cautioned Xiangyun and Baochai, “Neither of you two should eat too much. Crab may taste good, but it is not wholesome. If you eat too much, you will get a stomachache.” The two promptly assented and escorted her out of the garden. They then returned and ordered the remains of the feast cleared away and a fresh table laid. Baoyu said, “There is no need to set the tables again. Let us write poetry first. Just leave the large round table in the center, with all the wine and food upon it. There is no need to assign seats. Anyone who wants something can help themselves. Would it not be more convenient for everyone to sit where they please?” Baochai said, “That is an excellent idea.” Xiangyun said, “That may be so, but there are others to consider.” She therefore ordered another table to be laid, selected some hot crabs, and invited Xiren, Zijuan, Siqi, Daishu, Ruhua, Yinger, Cuimo, and the others to sit and eat together. Two flower-patterned rugs were spread beneath the osmanthus trees on the hillside, and the matrons and young maids who were on duty were told to sit there too and eat and drink as they pleased, returning only when they were summoned.

p.src: Xiangyun took the list of poetry topics and pinned it to the wall with a needle. When the others had read it, they all said, “Novel it certainly is, but we fear the poems may prove impossible to compose.” Xiangyun again explained why no rhyme scheme had been prescribed. Baoyu said, “That is the proper way. I have never liked prescribed rhymes either.” Since Lin Daiyu drank little wine and ate no crabs, she had an embroidered stool placed by the balustrade, where she sat fishing with a rod. Baochai toyed for a while with a spray of osmanthus, then leaned over the windowsill, pinched off some tiny blossoms, and tossed them onto the water, enticing the fish to rise and nibble at the surface. Xiangyun would lapse into thought, then urge Xiren and the others to eat, and call to everyone below the slope to help themselves without restraint. Tanchun, Li Wan, and Xichun stood in the shade of the drooping willows watching the gulls and egrets. Yingchun stood alone beneath the flowering boughs, threading jasmine blossoms with a flower needle. Baoyu watched Daiyu fish for a while, then leaned over beside Baochai to exchange a few laughing words; next he watched Xiren and the others eat crabs and joined them for a couple of cups of wine. Xiren picked the meat from another shell for him to eat. Daiyu laid down her fishing rod and went over to the seats. She picked up the black-silver self-pouring winepot decorated with plum blossoms and chose a tiny banana-leaf-shaped cup of frozen-stone agate patterned like begonia. Seeing this, a maid realized that she wanted wine and hurried forward to pour it for her. Daiyu said, “Go and enjoy your food. Let me pour for myself—that will be more amusing.” As she spoke, she poured half a cup, but on looking found that it was yellow wine. “I ate a little crab,” she said, “and now I feel a slight pain in my chest. I must have a hot sip of spirits.” Baoyu hastily said, “We have spirits.” He ordered a pot of wine infused with silk-tree blossoms to be warmed. Daiyu took only one sip before setting it down. Baochai came over too, took another cup, and had a sip. Then she dipped the brush in ink, went to the wall, marked off the first topic, “Remembering Chrysanthemums,” and added the character “Heng” beneath it. Baoyu cried, “Dear cousin, I already have four lines for the second topic. Please leave that one to me.” Baochai laughed. “I have only just managed to compose one, yet see how anxious you are already.” Without a word, Daiyu took the brush and marked off the eighth topic, “Questioning Chrysanthemums,” and then the eleventh, “Dreaming of Chrysanthemums,” adding the character “Xiao” beneath them. Baoyu also took up the brush, marked off the second topic, “Visiting Chrysanthemums,” and added the character “Jiang.” Tanchun came over to look and said, “No one has chosen ‘Wearing Chrysanthemums.’ Let me compose that one.” Then, pointing at Baoyu, she laughed and said, “It was just announced that no boudoir expressions were to appear, so mind what you write.”

p.src: As she spoke, Shi Xiangyun came over and marked off both the fourth and fifth topics, “Facing Chrysanthemums” and “Displaying Chrysanthemums,” adding the character “Xiang” beneath them. Tanchun said, “You ought to choose a sobriquet too.” Xiangyun laughed. “Although our family now has several halls and pavilions, I do not live in any of them, so borrowing a name from one would be pointless.” Baochai laughed. “Just now the Old Lady said that your family also had a waterside pavilion called Sunset-Mist Pavilion. Surely it belonged to you. Though it is gone now, you were its former mistress, after all.” Everyone agreed that this made sense. Before Xiangyun could act, Baoyu rubbed out the character “Xiang” for her and replaced it with “Xia.” After about the time it takes to eat a meal, all twelve topics had been completed. Each poem was copied out and handed to Yingchun, who took another sheet of Snow-Wave paper and transcribed them all together, noting each author’s sobriquet beneath that person’s work. Tanchun said, “You ought to choose a sobriquet too.”
Xiangyun laughed. “Although our family now has several halls and pavilions, I do not live in any of them, so borrowing a name from one would be pointless.”
Baochai laughed. “Just now the Old Lady said that your family also had a waterside pavilion called Sunset-Mist Pavilion. Surely it belonged to you.
Though it is gone now, you were its former mistress, after all.”
Everyone agreed that this made sense. Before Xiangyun could act, Baoyu rubbed out the character “Xiang” for her and replaced it with “Xia.”

After about the time it takes to eat a meal, all twelve topics had been completed. Each poem was copied out and handed to Yingchun, who took another sheet of Snow-Wave paper and transcribed them all together, noting each author’s sobriquet beneath that person’s work.

p.src: They read and praised each poem in turn, endlessly extolling one another's work. Li Wan laughed. “Let me give an impartial judgment. Taken as a whole, every poem has its own striking lines. My verdict today is that ‘In Praise of Chrysanthemums’ comes first, ‘Questioning the Chrysanthemum’ second, and ‘A Dream of Chrysanthemums’ third. Their subjects are novel, their verses novel, and their conceptions newer still, so we cannot help but crown the Xiaoxiang Consort our champion. Next come ‘Wearing Chrysanthemums,’ ‘Facing Chrysanthemums,’ ‘Displaying Chrysanthemums,’ ‘Painting Chrysanthemums,’ and ‘Remembering Chrysanthemums.’” Baoyu clapped his hands in delight. “Exactly! Perfectly fair!” Daiyu said, “My poem is not so good either. It is rather too delicate and contrived.” “Its ingenuity is precisely what makes it good,” said Li Wan. “It never seems labored or stiff.” Daiyu said, “To my mind, the finest opening line is ‘In the chilly garden at sunset, I recall old excursions.’ It applies the powder from the reverse side. ‘Casting aside my book, I face a single branch of autumn’ is already exquisite beyond compare and says all there is to say about displaying chrysanthemums. With nowhere further to go, the poet turns back to imagine the flowers before they were cut and set out; the thought has great depth.” Li Wan laughed. “That is true, but your line about ‘a mouth holding fragrance’ is every bit its equal.” Tanchun added, “Still, Lady Hengwu's composure must be acknowledged. With ‘autumn leaves no trace’ and ‘dreams possess awareness,’ she has brought the very word ‘remember’ vividly to life.” Baochai laughed. “And your ‘chilled against short sidelocks’ and ‘fragrance staining a hempen kerchief’ describe wearing chrysanthemums so completely that not the smallest gap remains.” Xiangyun said, “‘With whom will you hide away?’ and ‘Why are you so late?’ truly question the chrysanthemum until it has no answer left to give.” Li Wan laughed. “But with your ‘sitting bareheaded’ and ‘chanting with knees clasped,’ you never leave the chrysanthemums even for a moment. If they had feelings, they would surely be tired of you.” At this, everyone laughed. Baoyu laughed. “I have failed the examination again! Surely ‘At whose home were you planted?’ ‘Where does autumn dwell?’ ‘Coming from afar in waxed clogs,’ and ‘Endlessly chanting in the cold’ all count as seeking; and surely ‘last night's rain’ and ‘this morning's frost’ count as planting? I merely regret that they cannot match such lines as ‘With fragrance held between my lips, I chant to the moon,’ ‘In the pure cold fragrance, I clasp my knees and chant,’ ‘short sidelocks,’ ‘hempen kerchief,’ ‘golden petals serenely pale,’ ‘green leaves hanging disheveled,’ ‘autumn leaves no trace,’ and ‘dreams possess awareness.’” Then he added, “When I have time tomorrow, I shall compose all twelve by myself.” Li Wan said, “Yours are good too; they simply lack the novel ingenuity of those lines.”
